what: Hardware: one NVIDIA L4 (23 GB; about a third of the RTX 4090's memory bandwidth) instead of the planned RTX A4500. Measured decode latency was 89 ms/step at B=20 and 101 ms/step at B=40, so batches are B=40 rows instead of B=10.
consequence: Batch shape is constant within each shape class (task, cache length, first position); CRN partners of a slot always meet identical kernels (U1 = 1.00, U2 = 1.00).

what: Rows of different templates with equal prompt length share a batch (cross-template packing); the last batch of a class is padded with discarded duplicate rows.
consequence: None on the estimates; rows never interact inside a batch.

what: V1 (one-shot veto) runs at N=100 (k 0-19) instead of N=50; VP (persistent veto) at N=100 on the path screen; route arms c/d also run on non-gated tasks at N=100 (descriptive, Q5 upgraded).
consequence: More precision at no extra batch cost (B=40 pairs b with V1, a with c, etc.).

what: K0 is implemented by removing the condition span [p0, p1) from the cache instead of masking it (keys keep their RoPE rotation; generated queries keep positions P + step).
consequence: Exact for every generated query; checked in U3 against exp8's masked knockout (TV distance 1.2e-7 on the first generated position; eager attention mass on the span exactly 0 in all 36 layers). Lets every batch run stock SDPA with native GQA.

what: A row stops once its first fenced code block is closed (both labellers extract exactly that block).
Memory guard: finished rows are pruned from a batch once it passes step 560 (B=40 would otherwise exceed the L4's memory at ~600 new tokens).
consequence: Only rows still running past step 560 change batch shape after that step; their CRN coupling is approximate after it (logged per row as pruned_at).

what: Order: the ban-free arms (S4 b/V1, path screen round 1, twin-only controls pl/bB/K0b) ran before the analysis code was appended to commit #1, and before the T2 engine tests U1-U3/U9; no ban prompt of any task was sampled before commit #1 closed (asserted in code).
consequence: The decision rules and thresholds were already frozen in predictions/prereg.md (commit #1, first lines); the analysis code itself was committed after ban-free outputs existed.

what: Placebo splice (pl vs b under noun B) and K0b ran on the first three Stage-A tasks (T03, T04, T06) before the gate was known (the plan says the first three GATED tasks).
consequence: They are splice- and knockout-mechanics controls, valid whatever the gate.

what: Judge: the frozen bench judge j1 (gemini-2.5-flash-lite) hit transient HTTP 429 limits; failed calls are retried with backoff and rows left 'disputed' are re-judged when the label worker is idle (corrected rows appended; readers take the last row per uid). Caps: USD 0.15 per judge family (bench j1 + exp8 suite judge), total <= USD 0.30.
consequence: Rows still disputed at the end are excluded from shares (F7) and reported.

what: Proximity uses Zhang-Shasha (zss) on AST trees whose node labels are node types (user identifiers normalised; attribute names and constant types kept).
consequence: Used only in the secondary C1 rows.

what: U4-U6 (veto prefix identity, persistent-veto absence, prefill verbatim) are checked on all production rows by audit/rederive.py rather than on a separate 20-slot test.

Label-worker restarts (to add judge retries and lower the judge caps) killed the wrapper subshell instead of the Python process, so from 18:50 to 20:16 UTC up to three label workers ran concurrently and each labelled the same rows. data/samples.jsonl therefore accumulated duplicate rows (24,924 lines for 13,030 uids); it was compacted to the last row per uid, which is the row every reader (GPU queue, commit #2, analysis, audit) used throughout.
consequence: Labels come from the same frozen labellers with code-hash caches, so duplicates agree up to judge nondeterminism on a few judge-labelled programs; the audit re-derives commit #2's V_t within 0.02 and finds 0 mismatches. Some judge calls were duplicated; total judge spend stayed at USD 0.105.

what: The bench pilot was generated with Qwen3-8B-FP8 in vLLM; this artifact samples bf16 weights in HF transformers (as planned).
consequence: Arm-b default shares are 0.95 (T03), 0.76 (R6), 0.92 (T14) instead of the pilot's ~1.0; the distinctive n-gram was frozen on the pilot programs.
